_about: Version 2 short-form videos (see studio/shorts.py). `calendar` is the publishing order; the scheduled run takes the first id not yet sent. Ids: MQ-Q quotation, MQ-I interactive question, MQ-A activity, MQ-M common mistake. Quotation scenes take their text from curriculum/quotes.json and never restate it. Other ideas must cite published Money Quest content in `sources`.

videos.cover_title: Can 50p a week reach a big goal?
videos.hook: Can 50p a week reach a big goal?

scenes.text: Start a savings jar together. Add a little every week.
What is your child saving for?

videos.description: “Little strokes fell great oaks.” Benjamin Franklin, The Way to Wealth, 1758. Small, regular savings are how children reach a big goal. Try a savings jar and add to it every week. What is your child saving for? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Would your child save £5 or spend it?
videos.hook: Would your child save £5 or spend it?

scenes.text: Their reason shows how they think about money.
Ask tonight. Listen first, then say what you would do.
What did your child choose?

videos.description: Would your child save £5, spend it or split it? There is no wrong answer. Ask tonight, and ask why. Their reason shows how they think about money. Tell us what your child chose. Teaching children about money with Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

sources.quote: ask what they'd do with a fixed amount of money before telling them what you'd do
There is more than one reasonable choice.

videos.cover_title: A 2-minute money game for your next shop
videos.hook: Try this game on your next shop.

scenes.text: Pick two packs of the same thing.
Read the weight on each label.
Ask your child: which one gives more?
A bigger box can hold less. Let them check.
Save this idea for your next shop.

videos.description: A 2-minute money game for the supermarket. Pick two packs, read the weight on each label and ask your child which one gives more. A bigger box can hold less, and children enjoy finding out. Save this for your next shop. Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

sources.quote: A package can look bigger while holding less. Compare the same units on the labels.

videos.cover_title: How do you raise a responsible child?
videos.hook: How do you raise a responsible child?

scenes.text: Give one real job this week, and trust them with it.
Which job could your child own?

videos.description: “Few things help an individual more than to place responsibility upon him, and to let him know that you trust him.” Booker T. Washington, Up from Slavery, 1901. Washington wrote this about running a school, and it holds for a family too. A small, real responsibility, given with trust, is one of the simplest ways to help a child grow. Which job could your child own? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Why does that toy feel so urgent right now?
videos.hook: Why does that toy feel so urgent right now?

scenes.text: Before buying, wait one day. Then ask if they still want it.
Would your child still want it tomorrow?

videos.description: “Nothing in life is as important as you think it is, while you are thinking about it.” Daniel Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow, 2011. In the moment, the thing a child wants can feel like the only thing that matters. Adults feel it too. A short pause before deciding is a habit worth practising together. Would your child still want it tomorrow? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Is your child afraid of getting it wrong?
videos.hook: Is your child afraid of getting it wrong?

scenes.text: Praise the try, then ask what they would change.
What did your child learn from a mistake?

videos.description: “We often discover what will do, by finding out what will not do; and probably he who never made a mistake never made a discovery.” Samuel Smiles, Self-Help, 1859. Every young inventor needs to hear this. An idea that doesn't work is information, not failure. Children learn to create by testing small ideas and trying again. What did your child learn from a mistake? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Why do small things feel so big to children?
videos.hook: Why do small things feel so big to children?

scenes.text: Name the feeling together before you fix the problem.
Which feeling is hardest for your child?

videos.description: “Men are disturbed not by the things which happen, but by the opinions about the things.” Epictetus, The Encheiridion, trans. George Long. An idea almost two thousand years old: what we tell ourselves about an event shapes how it feels. Children can learn to notice a feeling and choose a next step. Which feeling is hardest for your child? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: What does that toy really cost your child?
videos.hook: What does that toy really cost your child?

scenes.text: Count the cost in weeks of pocket money.
How many weeks would it take?

videos.description: “The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run.” Henry David Thoreau, Walden, 1854. Thoreau measured cost in life, not money: the time and effort something takes to earn. It's a useful question for a child weighing a purchase against a savings goal. How many weeks would it take? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Which skill will your child always need?
videos.hook: Which skill will your child always need?

scenes.text: Let your child teach you one thing they learned.
What did your child teach you?

videos.description: “The object and reward of learning is continued capacity for growth.” John Dewey, Democracy and Education, 1916. For Dewey, the point of learning was the ability to keep learning. That matters even more for children growing up with tools that change every year. What did your child teach you? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Can one coin a week change a habit?
videos.hook: Can one coin a week change a habit?

scenes.text: Pick one tiny money habit and repeat it weekly.
Which small habit will you start?

videos.description: “Every action you take is a vote for the type of person you wish to become.” James Clear, Atomic Habits, 2018. A coin in a jar is a small thing. Repeated every week, it becomes evidence a child can point to: "I'm someone who saves." Which small habit will you start? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Why do early habits matter so much?
videos.hook: Why do early habits matter so much?

scenes.text: Tie a new habit to something you already do.
Which routine works in your home?

videos.description: “The great thing in all education is to make our nervous system our ally instead of our enemy.” William James, Talks to Teachers on Psychology, 1899. William James argued that habits do much of the work for us, for better or worse. Small routines practised in childhood, like saving a coin or checking a list, become things a child no longer has to think about. Which routine works in your home? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: How do children learn to trust themselves?
videos.hook: How do children learn to trust themselves?

scenes.text: Let your child make one real choice today.
What did they decide?

videos.description: “Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.” Ralph Waldo Emerson, Self-Reliance, 1841. Self-trust isn't something we can hand to a child. It comes from making real decisions and seeing what happens, ideally where mistakes cost nothing. What did they decide? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Are you doing too much for your child?
videos.hook: Are you doing too much for your child?

scenes.text: Hand over one task, then step back.
Which task will you hand over?

videos.description: “No one can be free unless he is independent.” Maria Montessori, The Montessori Method, 1912. Montessori saw independence as the first goal of education. At home it can start small: one job, one decision, one thing a child manages alone. Which task will you hand over? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: How do you raise a kind child?
videos.hook: How do you raise a kind child?

scenes.text: Ask your child who they could help this week.
Who did your child choose to help?

videos.description: “No one is useless in this world who lightens the burden of it for any one else.” Charles Dickens, Our Mutual Friend, 1865. A line from Dickens that children understand straight away: helping someone matters. Giving time, a toy or a little money is a habit that can start young. Who did your child choose to help? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Is money in charge, or is your child?
videos.hook: Is money in charge, or is your child?

scenes.text: Give a small amount and let them plan it.
What was their plan?

videos.description: “Money is in some respects like fire; it is a very excellent servant but a terrible master.” P. T. Barnum, The Art of Money Getting, 1880. Barnum's image still works: money is useful when you direct it. Children can practise being the one in charge, with small amounts and real choices. What was their plan? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: What do you say after your child's mistake?
videos.hook: What do you say after your child's mistake?

scenes.text: After a mistake, ask what they would try tomorrow.
Save this for the next hard day.

videos.description: “Isn't it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet?” L. M. Montgomery, Anne of Green Gables, 1908. Anne says this after a very bad day. It's a kind thing to tell a child, and a useful one: tomorrow is a chance to try differently. Save this for the next hard day. Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: Does your child memorise, or understand?
videos.hook: Does your child memorise, or understand?

scenes.text: Ask "why do you think that?" once a day.
What was the best answer you heard?

videos.description: “Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous.” Confucius, The Analects, trans. James Legge. Facts without thinking don't stick, and opinions without facts go wrong. Asking a child "why do you think that?" trains both at once. What was the best answer you heard? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

videos.cover_title: What is the simplest budget rule of all?
videos.hook: What is the simplest budget rule of all?

scenes.text: Try spending a little less than the pocket money.
Would you try this at home?

videos.description: “Annual income twenty pounds, annual expenditure nineteen nineteen and six, result happiness.” Charles Dickens, David Copperfield, 1850. Mr. Micawber's rule is the whole of budgeting in one line: spend slightly less than comes in. Children can practise it with pocket money long before they earn a wage. Would you try this at home? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.

scenes.text: A strong want can feel as urgent as a need.

videos.description: Need or want? Ask your child this. At the shop, ask what happens if you don't get it. What does your child call a need? Money lessons for children at Money Quest Academy, link in bio.
